title_translit: Harma Ba Par Jivanji Maharajni Krupa
title_en: Jivanji Maharaj's Grace upon Harma Ba
translation:
While traveling to Chorenda with a company of saints, Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj rested beneath a dry peepal tree on the bank of the pond in the village of Dhanora. Men sent by order of the village headman to cut down the peepal tree saw that it had turned green, and carried the news back to the village. The villagers and the headman, filled with reverence, came to have darshan of the saints and of Jivanji Maharaj, and made their request. This event is recorded in handwritten manuscript no. 28, pages 95 to 97, as follows: Jivandasji Maharaj came to Dhanora on his way from Chanderi to Chorenda. Jivandasji arrived at Dhanora. While travelling to Chorenda for the Sharad-night festival, the village of Dhanora came on the way. There, Jivandasji and the other Vaishnavs were seated together by the pond, beneath a peepal tree, and hari-kirtan was being sung. Now that peepal tree was dry. Because it had dried up, the village headman sent men to cut it down. At that, Jivandasji said that the peepal was in fact green and should not be cut; moreover, the Gitaji itself says that a peepal tree should not be cut — this is stated in the Gita, chapter 9, verse 10. The men then went back and reported that the peepal had indeed turned green.

On hearing this, all the villagers came at once to have darshan of the saints, and the moment they did, everyone's mind grew clear and pure. They asked, "This peepal was dry — how did it turn green?" Jivandasji replied that this peepal had dried up because of the bones of an ungrateful man, and that, likewise, water no longer remained in the pond either. He then spoke this sakhi (couplet) on the matter:

_Kritaghnike haadsu peepal sooko jaay,_
_so Jeevan leelo kiyo Sadguru tane pasaay. ||1||_
(Because of the bones of an ungrateful man this peepal had dried up; that same tree Jivan[a] made green again, by the grace granted by the Sadguru.)

Then they understood that some great soul had come to their village, and with this understanding they made a request: "This young woman is disabled from birth, and belongs to our own family." They brought the girl and placed her at his feet, whereupon Jivanji Maharaj showed his grace.

He told one attendant, "Go and bring water from the pond." The attendant took the kamandal (water vessel) and went to fetch water, but found no water at all in the pond, and returned. He told the Maharaj that there was no water in the pond. Jivandasji then said, "Brothers, in this world, just as the peepal dried up because of the bones of an ungrateful man, so too there is no water in the pond — but by the glory of the saints, water shall appear." He sent the attendant a second time, telling him to go and bring water from the pond. By the glory of the saints, water appeared there.

_Adhik badhaavat aapate, jan mahima Raghuveer,_
_Savari pad raj prasartaan, shuddh bhayo sarita neer. ||2||_
(Lord Raghuveer magnifies the glory of His devotee even more than His own; just as when the dust of Shabari's feet touched the river, its water became pure.)

In this way the water appeared, and the attendant brought it and gave it to the Maharaj. He took that water, sprinkled it upon the young woman's body, and also gave her some to drink; by this her disability left her body and she became whole, and moreover the light of true knowledge dawned in her.

Harmabai's Words

_Harmaanbai harkhiyaan, Jeevan darshan paay,_
_Shareere saanso mitiyo, bhayo gnaan prakaash. ||3||_
(Harmabai rejoiced on receiving the darshan of Jivan[a]; the affliction in her body was removed, and the light of true knowledge dawned.)

Harmabai's Words

_Gnaan prakaashi guru milyaa, so kem visaryo jaay,_
_Jo Govind kripa kare, to guru milenge aay. ||4||_
(The Guru who met me and lit the lamp of knowledge — how could he ever be forgotten? If Govind bestows His grace, that Guru will surely come and meet again.)

On hearing this sakhi, Jivanji Maharaj felt great joy, and understanding that this was some meritorious soul, he placed his hand upon her head — and at once her disability left her. Seeing this, Harmaba's father, Ratansinh, said, "I offer my daughter to you." Hearing this, Jivanji Maharaj said that they were wanderers who roamed from land to land, and that this would not befit a life of renunciation. The other devotees of the Guru who were present then persuaded Jivandasji.

Word of this also reached Gopaldasji in Chorenda, and he too said that this was indeed the wish of the Gracious Lord — that he should enter into worldly life (grihasth ashram). Jivandasji then agreed. Harmaba, moreover, said:

_Tumkun chhod avar kahaan jaau, nishadin tumhaari sang rahaavun._
(Leaving You, where else could I go? Day and night I shall remain in Your company.)

Hearing these words of Harmaba, he accepted her — just as Jagannath Swami had once given Padmavati to Jaydevji. In this way, by Hari's will, he accepted Harmaba, and himself stayed on for one month, singing hari-kirtan. He gave everyone knowledge (upadesh/teaching) and dispelled their ignorance. He then told Harmaba, "I shall travel with Gopaldasji through Malwa, Jagannathji, Naimisharanya, Kashi, Ayodhya, Mathura, and Badrikashram, and when I return I shall take care of you" — and having said this, he himself departed for Chorenda.
